source: Erickson Schultz Crone 2025 Ecosphere doi:10.1002/ecs2.70259; Figshare 10.6084/m9.figshare.25648644.v1; Milkweed_dat_with_coords_DEC2024.csv; source GitHub run 37735892534
disclosed_prior_view: 4518 source rows, 2022 unstratified egg and late instar totals, 131 paired route-month groups, 88 with events on both host origins, preliminary 2022 pooled MH odds ratio 0.414; seasonal M-H ORs spring 3.870 summer 0.174 fall 0.133. This is not independent confirmatory preregistration.
panel: 2022 source data for 15 urban routes, complete Eggs and Instar_1 to Instar_5, Num_plants>0, native vs exotic statuses
primary: Native/exotic difference in late(Instar_4+Instar_5) vs egg stage composition from Mantel-Haenszel odds ratio for exotic/native within same Route x calendar month strata, both plant origins present and each status having >=1 recorded egg/late event.

bootstrap.method: Resample entire routes with replacement (not eggs or plants), retaining their month x origin data

secondary.interaction: Spring versus fall log-odds-ratio contrast and route-bootstrap CI
secondary.stages: all larvae vs eggs; early Instar1+2 vs eggs; Instar5 vs eggs
secondary.observation_access: Exclude patches with explicit Too_far strings not blank or No
secondary.robustness: leave-one-route-out, 2023 incomplete-period sensitivity; no 2024 confirmatory inference

limits: Stage counts are distinct cross-sectional eggs and larvae, NOT tracked survival from egg to adult
Exotic/native status is confounded with milkweed species, phenology, foliage, accessibility and planting sites
Individual egg-level Mantel-Haenszel p values are anti-conservative under repeated patch and route sampling
Published source already analyzed seasonal larva:egg patterns; this is post-hoc reanalysis
Do not update GEB main manuscript
